title: Build an Event List Planner
summary: Build a complete event-list pipeline cumulatively: records, reusable functions, filtering, mapping, and final iteration.

sketchBlocks.title: Move from structured records to useful output
Keep each project step working before adding the next
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
The Event List Planner grows cumulatively:

**Step 1 — Model the schedule.** Build an array of event objects so each event keeps its name, category, and location together.

**Step 2 — Name two reusable decisions.** One function will answer whether an event belongs to the Technology category. Another will turn an event object into readable text.

**Step 3 — Compose the planner.** Filter the events, map the selected records to labels, then use `for...of` to display each line.

Each step begins with the complete working solution from the previous step. Do not throw away earlier code and rebuild from scratch. That cumulative workflow is how larger programs become manageable.

quizDraft.title: Step 1: Start the event collection
quizDraft.prompt: Problem: The event planner cannot process a schedule until each event is represented as one structured record. Task: Create `events` as an array containing one event object with `name`, `category`, and `location`. Expected result: Check Answer confirms one correctly shaped event record; the Console stays unchanged.
quizDraft.hint: Start with one complete record before growing the collection.

help.hint_1: Use one object inside the array.

quizDraft.title: Step 2: Complete the schedule data
quizDraft.prompt: Problem: One event is not enough to test a real planner, especially filtering across different categories. Task: Keep the first event and add three more event objects with the same `name`, `category`, and `location` shape. Expected result: Check Answer confirms a four-event collection with consistent records; the Console stays unchanged.
quizDraft.hint: Preserve the first object and repeat the same record shape.

quizDraft.prompt: Problem: The planner will need to select only Technology events, so it first needs one reusable yes-or-no rule for a single event. Task: Keep the complete event array and add only `isTechnology(event)` returning whether the category equals `Technology`. Expected result: Check Answer confirms the reusable category predicate; the Console stays unchanged.

quizDraft.title: Step 4: Format one event
quizDraft.prompt: Problem: Event objects are useful for code, but a student reading a schedule needs a short line with the event name and location. Task: Keep the data and predicate and add only `formatEvent(event)` returning `name — location`. Expected result: Check Answer confirms one event can be turned into a readable schedule line; the Console stays unchanged.
quizDraft.hint: Transform one record into one display string.

help.hint_2: Use event.location in the same template literal.

Task: Keep every previous function and add only `selectedEvents = events.filter(isTechnology)`. Expected result: Check Answer confirms the collection now has a Technology-only subset; the Console stays unchanged.
